title: Hyrkanos, Son of R' Eliezer ben Hyrkanos

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Shabbat 147a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.147a.6), going out on Shabbat with a scarf on his shoulder; and in [Menachot 35a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.35a.8), tying his tefillin with straps of purple wool, and [his father] said nothing to him. In [Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 3:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.3.4.7), Hyrkanos said to Rabbi Eliezer: “By refusing to answer her a single word of Torah, you have cost me three hundred kor of tithe every year.”

[Sanhedrin 68a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.68a.2) relates that when R-A fell ill, his son Hyrkanos went in on Shabbat eve to remove his father’s tefillin. R-A rebuked him, and Hyrkanos left after the rebuke. Hyrkanos said to his colleagues (those of R-A), “It seems to me that my father’s mind is confused.” R-A replied, “His mind and his mother’s mind are confused.” On the She’iltot’s reading in Shemot, Hyman identifies him with the Hyrkanos mentioned in [Shabbat 127b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.127b.5), whose father R-A consecrated all his property because his son Hyrkanos did not study Torah. In [Mishnah Yevamot 12:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Yevamot.12.6) we find: “When Rabbi Hyrkanos prompted the recitation under the terebinth in Kefar Etam (Hyman reports Kefar Aviyah in the [Jerusalem Talmud](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.12.6.1) [1]) and completed the whole section, they established the practice of completing the whole section.” Hyman says the identification with the son of R-A requires investigation, since the son is mentioned everywhere without the title “Rabbi.”[^5]

notes.text: The footnote marker1 has no supplied footnote, and Hyman explicitly questions whether the Rabbi Hyrkanos in Yevamot is this otherwise untitled son; p002 remains held. ממגי is read as ממני. Eliezer, his son Hyrkanos and the cited mother remain distinct speakers and relatives.

The Wikisource note marked [1] suggests Avuhah (אבוה) and records Avus (אבוס) in its Jerusalem Talmud. Hyman’s printed notice reads Aviyah (אביה), without that footnote. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Mishnah has Kefar Avus, and the standalone Mishnah has Kefar Etam. The place variants leave Hyman’s identification question open.

The printed notice and Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 3:4 read “from me” (ממני). Shabbat 127b gives Hyrkanos as the son of an unnamed employer, who says he placed his property under a vow. She’iltot, Shemot 40, names the employer as Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrkanos and says he consecrated his property so that his son would study Torah.

[Menachot 35a:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.35a.8) explains the father’s silence by saying he did not see what his son did. [Shabbat 147a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.147a.6) gives the further detail that a thread was wrapped around Hyrkanos’s finger. [Heilprin’s entry on Hyrkanos](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1023&lang=en) includes both episodes and also lists the Kefar Etam passage. Hyman explicitly leaves the identification in that last passage open.
